subject.title: [Feature]: Support sessionKey-based concurrency guard for webhook       deliveries

question: Should hook-agent deliveries with the same resolved sessionKey be rejected, skipped, queued, or left parallel by default, and should a 409 conflict mode be opt-in?
rationale: The requested guard changes the external webhook response contract and retry behavior, so automation should not choose the default or compatibility policy without maintainer intent.

options.title: Add opt-in overlap policy
options.body: Keep current accepted-by-default behavior while allowing trusted hook mappings or direct hook calls to choose reject, skip, or queue semantics with documented retry behavior.

options.title: Make 409 the default
options.body: Reject same-session active deliveries by default and require existing integrations to migrate if they depend on 200/runId acceptance.

options.title: Keep caller-managed locking
options.body: Leave hook delivery admission unchanged and document idempotency keys plus client-side locks as the supported overlap control.

recommendation.title: Add opt-in overlap policy
recommendation.body: Keep current accepted-by-default behavior while allowing trusted hook mappings or direct hook calls to choose reject, skip, or queue semantics with documented retry behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest recent session-lifecycle and hook-runtime history for this compatibility-sensitive product boundary.
